record.original_question: Suppose that f in S and define ∞ X fp (z) = [f (z)]p = z p + an,p z n . n=p+1 What can be said about bounds for an,p ? If |an,1 | ≤ Kn for all n and fixed K, then, for integral p, 2p(2p + 1) . . . (n + p − 1) |an, p | ≤ K p , (n − p)! but it might be easier to obtain bounds for fp than for f . (W. K. Hayman)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ denote the class of functions $f$ that are holomorphic and univalent in the unit disk $\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ and normalized by $f(0)=0$, $f'(0)=1$, so that $f(z)=z+\sum_{n=2}^{\infty}a_n z^n$. For $p>0$, choose a single-valued branch of $[f(z)]^p$ near $z=0$ and write its power-series expansion as
$$f_p(z):=[f(z)]^p = z^p + \sum_{n=p+1}^{\infty} a_{n,p}\, z^n.$$
Determine sharp (or best possible) bounds for the coefficients $a_{n,p}$, valid for all $f\in S$, all $n>p$, and all $p>0$ (or, at least, all positive integers $p$).

It is known that the Bieberbach conjecture $|a_{n,1}|\le n$ holds (de Branges), and that this implies, for positive integers $p$,
$$|a_{n,p}|\le K^p\,\frac{2p\,(2p+1)\cdots(n+p-1)}{(n-p)!}$$
whenever $|a_{n,1}|\le Kn$ for all $n$ (with fixed constant $K$). The problem is to find the sharp asymptotic and explicit bounds for $|a_{n,p}|$, with the possibility that bounding $f_p$ directly may be more tractable than bounding $f$ itself.
artifact.status_search_result: Sharp bounds for the coefficients $a_{n,p}$ of powers of functions in $S$ remain a classical open problem in geometric function theory. While the Bieberbach conjecture $|a_n|\le n$ was proved by de Branges (1985), and Hayman's regularity theorem and various asymptotic results are known, no sharp universal bound for $|a_{n,p}|$ for all $p>0$ and all $n>p$ has been established. Related conjectures (e.g., on successive coefficients of odd univalent functions) have been resolved more recently, but the general question for powers $f_p$ remains open.

status_evidence.title: Bieberbach conjecture - Encyclopedia of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses de Branges' proof of |a_n|<=n and related coefficient problems for powers and means of univalent functions.
status_evidence.claim: The base case p=1 is settled by de Branges, but sharp bounds for general powers remain a classical question.

status_evidence.title: Univalent and Multivalent Functions (Hayman, Lingham)
status_evidence.snippet: Hayman obtained a number of results on the asymptotic behaviour of coefficients of functions p-sheeted in |z|<1.
status_evidence.claim: Hayman's results give asymptotics, not sharp bounds, for coefficients of powers.

status_evidence.title: Logarithmic coefficients and a coefficient conjecture for univalent functions
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to investigate coefficient conjectures for univalent functions and their relatives.
status_evidence.claim: Coefficient bounds for powers/logarithms of univalent functions are still actively studied.
